[claude] **Cross-module active-front count inconsistency on fallback paths**: When `_loop_state` is unavailable, `output_gate.py`'s `_fallback_protocol_state` parses `frontier.md` using `### H3` regex matching (only counts fronts defined as H3-level sections), while `run_gate.py`'s `_count_open_fronts` fallback reads all blocks with `Status:` fields (any section level). They could disagree on active front count if an operator uses H2-level front headings. Both would still block closure (output_gate through Coda enforcement, run_gate through open-front counting), so this creates defense-in-depth rather than a bypass, but the inconsistency is a latent maintenance risk.

[claude] **Deny-list nature of Coda vague-phrase detection**: The `vague_only` set and `vague_phrase` regex in `_turn_coda` (output_gate.diff lines 36-48) cover common Chinese evasion phrases, but Chinese has many semantically equivalent formulations. Phrases like "按计划推进", "沿当前路径深挖", "依照原定方向继续" could bypass the deny-list while being semantically vague. The concrete_anchor requirement (must reference an F-id, tool, or filename) provides a strong second layer — a vague Coda without a concrete anchor is rejected regardless. This layered approach is well-designed for this inherent limitation.

[claude] **No adversarial selftests for the `_fallback_protocol_state` frontier parser with unusual heading formats**: The selftest covers `### Front F-002 — login` (output_gate.diff line 321-322) but does not test edge cases like `### F-001 (was F-003)`, `### ## F-001`, or H3 headings where the F-id appears after the first 100 characters. The fallback is only activated when `loop_state` is unavailable, making this a narrow edge case with low exposure.

[claude] **The `_retro_framework_items` splitter (check_run.diff lines 118-127) correctly handles `Problem:` fields, numbered items, and heading-based items, but the fallback `return [body]` when no structure is found lumps all issues into one item — meaning one Status line discharges an entire free-form section. The disposition.md (lines 42-44) documents this as an intentional template tradeoff. The template now explicitly requires structured format (`docs.diff` retrospective template changes), which shifts enforcement from code to documentation. This is a reasonable design choice but means the gate's effectiveness depends on template compliance.
